cases.question: What expo was announced, when, and did admission cover competitions?
cases.query: SoCal Expo January free competitions
cases.answer: The interview announced the SoCal Retro Gaming Expo for January 30–31, 2016, in City of Industry, with 9 a.m.–5 p.m. hours both days. Steven says admission and all competitions would be free. It is a historical announcement, not a current event listing. The planned program included free play, a small history museum, a Star Fox competition and a professional Smash Bros. tournament.
cases.reason: P1–2/P5–6/P36–37 exact historical announced dates/free terms and planned activities, not completed/current event.

cases.question: Did Steven guarantee every vendor would have clean games?
cases.query: clean vendors retail standard
cases.answer: No. Steven promised an organized, professional environment but explicitly said he could not control what every vendor brought. He separately explained that retail should meet a higher standard, including cleaning and testing games so buyers can go home and play them. Johnny values that service and condition enough to pay a few dollars more.

cases.question: How did Steven's collecting become a store?
cases.query: Steven sweepstakes doubles hoarding laid off seven months company June 2008 Diamond Bar April
cases.answer: Steven recalls a childhood $2,000 Toys R Us sweepstakes win that helped him get Atari 2600 and NES hardware, and says he kept his collection and packaging. Later duplicate-buying supplied inventory. After a layoff, a new job and seven months there, he left to vend; he gives June 2008 as his booth opening. He later opened Super Video Game Bros in Diamond Bar in April of the prior year—April 2015 relative to this January 2016 episode. These are his recollections, not independently audited dates.

cases.reason: Full biography chronology P8–21 distinguishes childhood recollection, inventory, job change, June2008booth and relativeApril2015store date.
